_note: v2 hook overrides for le Chapiteau du Cirque (B55_cirque). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings).

fr_immediatement_adv.hook: Like English 'immediately', said ee-may-dyah-tuh-MAHN: the ringmaster cracks her whip and a little flower MEADOW bursts IMMEDIATELY out of the sawdust at her feet.
fr_immediatement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted ringmaster is a man; the flowers spring up beside him.

fr_parfaitement_adv.hook: Like English 'perfectly', said pahr-feh-tuh-MAHN: a girl balances a towering strawberry parfait ("pahr-FEH") on one hand, holding it PERFECTLY still on one leg.
fr_parfaitement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted girl balances the parfait on her hand, not her nose.

fr_particulierement_adv.hook: Like English 'particularly', said pahr-tee-kew-lyeh-ruh-MAHN: a picky white poodle is PARTICULARLY fond of one big black boot and hugs it close.
fr_particulierement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows the poodle with a single boot (no ringmaster).

fr_doucement_adv.hook: "doo-suh-MAHN": DEW-SO-MAN — the strongman lifts a dewy rose SO GENTLY that not one drop of DEW falls. doucement = gently.

fr_facilement_adv.hook: A strongman, a facile man ("fah-see-luh-MAHN"), lifts a baby elephant over his head EASILY, smiling.
fr_facilement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted strongman lifts the elephant with his arms, not one finger.

fr_naturellement_adv.hook: Like English 'naturally', said nah-tew-reh-luh-MAHN: a seal claps its flippers NATURALLY, as if it was born to perform.
fr_naturellement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no band is painted; the seal claps on its own.

fr_brusquement_adv.hook: Like English 'brusquely', said brews-kuh-MAHN: a clown BREWS tea on a drum, and SUDDENLY the teapot lid pops off in a puff of steam.
fr_brusquement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted teapot puffs steam as the lid pops; the clown pours onto a drum.

fr_rapidement_adv.hook: Like English 'rapidly', said rah-pid-MAHN: a unicycling clown zips RAPIDLY round the ring, arms flung wide and coat-tails flying.

fr_vite_adv.hook: A vet ("VEET") rushes QUICKLY over with his stethoscope to check the seal.
fr_vite_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the vet is painted beside the seal, stethoscope ready.

fr_mal_adv.hook: "MAHL": the clown's MALL shopping bags burst and his ice cream drops: everything goes BADLY. mal = badly.
fr_mal_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the malady is painted as a bandage round his head.

fr_directement_adv.hook: Like English 'directly', said dee-rehk-tuh-MAHN: a blindfolded clown walks DIRECTLY into the one cream pie on the stand: splat!

fr_soudain_adv.hook: Like English 'sudden', said soo-DAN: SUDDENLY Dan the clown springs up out of a trapdoor on a coil spring, and his partner Sue squeals "soo-DAN!"
fr_soudain_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the trapdoor is in the stand, and Dan pops up on a spring.

fr_debout_adv.hook: A ghost shouts "BOO!" ("duh-BOO") and the whole circus audience jumps up STANDING.

fr_tranquillement_adv.hook: Like English 'tranquilly', said trahn-kee-luh-MAHN: a lion naps CALMLY in a little wooden boat, resting his chin on its KEEL-side.
fr_tranquillement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted lion sleeps inside a boat, not on an upturned keel.

fr_d_abord_adv.hook: "All ABOARD!" ("da-BOR"): FIRST the red wagon, then the clowns climb on in line, one after the other. FIRST of all comes the wagon.
fr_d_abord_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a red circus wagon leading a queue of clowns (no teacher or board).

fr_ensemble_adv.hook: Like English 'ensemble', said ahn-SAHNBL: a whole clown ENSEMBLE squeezes into one tiny striped car TOGETHER.

fr_aussitot_adv.hook: "Oh, see toe!" ("oh-see-TOH"): a polka-dot clown stubs his toe and grabs it IMMEDIATELY, hopping on one foot.
fr_aussitot_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no plaster is painted; the clown grabs his foot at once.

fr_bien_adv.hook: A circus bee ("BYAN") juggles WELL, three coloured balls in the air and never a drop.

fr_justement_adv.hook: "JUST the man ("zhews-tuh-MAHN") I wanted: EXACTLY!" says the ringmaster, pointing as the juggler with his clubs arrives.

fr_lentement_adv.hook: A lantern man ("lahn-tuh-MAHN") walks SLOWLY behind a snail, step by tiny step.
fr_lentement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: a snail is painted at his feet to show the slowness.

fr_notamment_adv.hook: Like English 'notably', said noh-tah-MAHN: between two plain clowns one stands out NOTABLY: NO TAM o'shanter, MAN, he is dressed as a cabbage.
fr_notamment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted clown wears a cabbage costume between two others.

fr_simplement_adv.hook: Like English 'simply', said san-pluh-MAHN: a SAMPLE MAN in an apron SIMPLY holds up one cracker, proud as anything.
fr_simplement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted man holds the cracker up rather than tossing it.

fr_librement_adv.hook: LIBRA ("lee-bruh-MAHN"), the scales-man, juggles FREELY above his balancing scales, free as LIBERTY.

fr_soigneusement_adv.hook: A swan ("swah-nyeuh-zuh-MAHN") CAREFULLY balances an egg on top of its head.
fr_soigneusement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted egg sits on the swan's head, not its beak.

fr_violemment_adv.hook: Hear VIOLA in it ("vyoh-lah-MAHN"): a clown saws at his viola so VIOLENTLY that his hat flies off.
fr_violemment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the source hook described a wall text and a storm; the painting shows the clown with the viola.

fr_vivement_adv.hook: Like English 'vividly', said vee-vuh-MAHN: a girl KEENLY waves her flag at the ring, cheering "VIVE!" at every trick.

fr_volontiers_adv.hook: Like English 'volunteer', said voh-lohn-TYAY: a seal GLADLY VOLUNTEERS, flipper raised and a ball on its nose, while the clown holds up the hoop.
fr_volontiers_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted seal raises a flipper beside a clown with a hoop.

fr_attentivement_adv.hook: Like English 'attentively', said ah-tahn-tee-vuh-MAHN: a puppy watches ATTENTIVELY from the door of a little circus TENT, eyes on the juggling balls.

fr_discretement_adv.hook: Like English 'discreetly', said dees-kreh-tuh-MAHN: a clown hides a cream pie DISCREETLY behind him while the ringmaster looks the other way.

fr_durement_adv.hook: A dour man ("dur-MON") coaches HARSHLY, blowing his whistle as the clowns do press-ups.
fr_durement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the team is painted as clowns doing press-ups.

fr_gentiment_adv.hook: A gentle ("zhon-tee") clown KINDLY holds his umbrella over a granny and helps her along.
fr_gentiment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows an umbrella, not a door.

fr_joyeusement_adv.hook: Like English 'joyously', said zhwah-yeuh-zuh-MAHN: three seals balance beach balls JOYFULLY on their noses.
fr_joyeusement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no horns are painted.

fr_progressivement_adv.hook: Like English 'progressively', said proh-gray-see-vuh-MAHN: a GREY elephant edges along a low tightrope PROGRESSIVELY, one careful step after another.

fr_silencieusement_adv.hook: Like English 'silently', said see-lahn-syeuh-zuh-MAHN: a white-faced mime tiptoes SILENTLY across the ring, not a sound.
fr_silencieusement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no imaginary lance can be painted, so the mime simply tiptoes.

fr_bref_adv.hook: Like English 'brief', said BREHF: IN SHORT, the clown's speech is a scroll one line long, read in one BREATH.
fr_bref_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted clown reads from a short scroll.

fr_calmement_adv.hook: A calm man ("kahl-muh-MAHN") sits cross-legged and breathes CALMLY beside a bowl of perfectly still water.
fr_calmement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the still lake is painted as a still bowl of water beside a meditating clown.

fr_faiblement_adv.hook: A feeble old man ("feh-bluh-MON") lifts his teacup WEAKLY in both hands.

fr_nettement_adv.hook: A neat man ("net-MON") clips a poodle-shaped hedge NEATLY, every leaf in line.
fr_nettement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hedge is painted as a topiary poodle.

fr_patiemment_adv.hook: Like English 'patiently', said pah-syah-MAHN: PA in his flat cap fishes PATIENTLY in a bucket with one goldfish, waiting and waiting.
fr_patiemment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a man fishing in a bucket, not a ticket queue.

fr_tendrement_adv.hook: A tender clown ("tahn-druh-MAHN") hugs a sleepy kitten TENDERLY.

fr_difficilement_adv.hook: Like English 'with difficulty', said dee-fee-see-luh-MAHN: an elephant squeezes WITH DIFFICULTY through a hoop meant for poodles.

fr_largement_adv.hook: Not "largely" in sound: largement (lahr-zhuh-MAHN) means WIDELY, AMPLY; a LARGE hippo overflows a tiny bathtub on all sides.
fr_largement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a hippo in a tiny bath, not poppies.

fr_terriblement_adv.hook: Like English 'terribly', said teh-ree-bluh-MAHN: a monkey juggles plates TERRIBLY, and they crash and smash all around him.
fr_terriblement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted juggler is a monkey.

fr_forcement_adv.hook: NECESSARILY wet: the keeper stands right by the splashing seal "for sure, man" ("for-say-MON"), so he is NECESSARILY soaked.
fr_forcement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a seal soaking its keeper, not a man jumping into the sea.

fr_automatiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'automatically', said oh-toh-mah-tee-kuh-MAHN: the curtains swing open AUTOMATICALLY every time the lion sneezes.

fr_brutalement_adv.hook: Like English 'brutally', said brew-tah-luh-MAHN: a BRUTE of a bear bashes the drum BRUTALLY, sticks flying.
fr_brutalement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a bear bashing a drum, not a wave of water.

fr_desesperement_adv.hook: Like English 'desperately', said day-zehs-pay-ray-MAHN: RAY the clown searches DESPERATELY with a lantern for his red nose, and the seal beside him is wearing it.

fr_gravement_adv.hook: A giraffe is SERIOUSLY hurt, its neck in bandages, and a grave ("grav") vet hurries to help.
fr_gravement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the patient is painted as a giraffe.

fr_personnellement_adv.hook: Like English 'personally', said pehr-soh-neh-luh-MAHN: NELL PERSONALLY hands each penguin its own balloon.
fr_personnellement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted girl hands balloons to penguins.

fr_physiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'physically', said fee-zee-kuh-MAHN: a monkey gulps a FIZZY lemonade and is PHYSICALLY unable to stop doing handstands.
fr_physiquement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the acrobat is painted as a monkey beside the fizzy bottle.

fr_premierement_adv.hook: FIRSTLY, at the circus premiere ("pruh-MYAIR"), the lion walks the red carpet FIRST.
fr_premierement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the star on the red carpet is painted as a lion.

fr_principalement_adv.hook: Like English 'principally', said pran-see-pah-luh-MAHN: the circus is MAINLY run by a PRINCE and his PAL the poodle, side by side in the ticket booth.

fr_uniquement_adv.hook: Like English 'uniquely', said ew-nee-kuh-MAHN: a parrot eats ONLY the yellow sweets from the jar, picking them out one by one.
fr_uniquement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted sweet-picker is a parrot.

fr_fixement_adv.hook: A fixed stare ("feek-suh-MAHN"): a cat stares FIXEDLY at a goldfish bowl.
fr_fixement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted starer is a cat.

fr_legerement_adv.hook: A LEISURE-loving sloth ("lay-zhair-MON") in a hammock sways ever so SLIGHTLY.
fr_legerement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hammock sleeper is painted as a sloth.

fr_specialement_adv.hook: Like English 'specially', said spay-syah-luh-MAHN: a sea lion is given a fish cake with one candle, made SPECIALLY for him.
fr_specialement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a sea lion with a fish cake.

fr_bizarrement_adv.hook: Like English 'bizarrely', said bee-zah-ruh-MAHN: a bee in a top hat rides a unicycle, behaving most BIZARRELY for a bee.

fr_expres_adv.hook: ON PURPOSE, a monkey hops onto the red express ("eks-PRESS") train, grinning.
fr_expres_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the passenger is painted as a monkey.

fr_abondamment_adv.hook: Kids cry "A BUN, da man!" ("ah-bohn-dah-MAHN") as a jolly baker tosses warm buns ABUNDANTLY from his basket.
fr_abondamment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the buns come from a basket, as painted.

fr_courageusement_adv.hook: Like English 'courageously', said koo-rah-zheuh-zuh-MAHN: a clown dives COURAGEOUSLY into a tub of custard.

fr_fidelement_adv.hook: Like English 'faithfully', said fee-deh-luh-MAHN: a poodle follows the ringmaster FAITHFULLY, step for step.

fr_follement_adv.hook: A man ("MAHN") leaps MADLY in front of a picture of a garden folly ("fo-luh"), arms flapping.
fr_follement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the folly is painted as a picture behind him.

fr_joliment_adv.hook: A jolly man ("zhoh-lee-MAHN") arranges flowers PRETTILY in a vase.

fr_timidement_adv.hook: Like English 'timidly', said tee-mee-duh-MAHN: a little lion cub peeks TIMIDLY from behind a red curtain, blushing.

fr_adroitement_adv.hook: Like English 'adroitly', said ah-drwah-tuh-MAHN: a bear juggles ADROITLY on a unicycle, never dropping a ball.

fr_chaleureusement_adv.hook: A man offers a rose ("shah-leuh-REUHZ-mahn") to a girl beside the warm stove and greets her WARMLY.
fr_chaleureusement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a rose offered beside a stove; the source hook used a person's name.

fr_couramment_adv.hook: A swimmer glides FLUENTLY with the current ("koo-ra-MAHN"), smooth as can be.
fr_couramment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no speech can be painted, so only the gliding swimmer is used.

fr_durablement_adv.hook: Like English 'durably', said dew-rah-bluh-MAHN: elephants bounce in a safety net built so DURABLY that it never tears.
fr_durablement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows elephants on a sturdy net, not a tent in a storm.

fr_habilement_adv.hook: A very ABLE carpenter ("a-beel-MAHN") carves a wooden swan SKILFULLY, chips flying.

fr_impatiemment_adv.hook: Like English 'impatiently', said an-pah-syah-MAHN: a lion holds up his hoop and waits IMPATIENTLY for the act to start.
fr_impatiemment_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted lion holds the hoop himself.

fr_irremediablement_adv.hook: Like English 'irreparably', said ee-ray-may-dyah-bluh-MAHN: a clown tumbles as his stilts smash into pieces, broken IRREPARABLY.
fr_irremediablement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows smashed wooden stilts, not a clown car.

fr_solidement_adv.hook: Like English 'solidly', said soh-lee-duh-MAHN: a strongwoman holds the ladder SOLIDLY while an acrobat stands on top.
fr_solidement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: one acrobat is painted at the top.

fr_loyalement_adv.hook: Like English 'loyally', said lwah-yah-luh-MAHN: a dog sits LOYALLY at the foot of the ladder, looking up at her acrobat friend.

fr_affreusement_adv.hook: A snowman is DREADFULLY frozen ("ah-FREUH-zuh MAHN"), shivering HORRIBLY with icicles hanging off him.

fr_delicatement_adv.hook: Like English 'delicately', said day-lee-kah-tuh-MAHN: a deli cat in a striped apron DELICATELY steadies a wobbling tower of eggs.
fr_delicatement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted cat stands by the egg tower on a stool, not on a high wire.

fr_froidement_adv.hook: The Snow Queen frowns ("FRWAHD-mahn") at a little man and glares COLDLY, icicles in the air.

fr_horriblement_adv.hook: Like English 'horribly', said oh-ree-bluh-MAHN: a trumpet plays HORRIBLY out of tune, and two seals cover their ears with their flippers.

fr_inutilement_adv.hook: A man ("MON") waters a plant sealed under a glass dome: quite USELESSLY, of no utility ("ee-nu-teel"), the water just runs off into a puddle.
fr_inutilement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a glass dome over the plant rather than a plastic plant.

fr_moralement_adv.hook: Like English 'morally', said moh-rah-luh-MAHN: a clown finds a wallet and, MORALLY sure, hands it straight back to the smiling lady.

fr_poliment_adv.hook: Like English 'politely', said poh-lee-MAHN: a gentleman tips his top hat POLITELY.

fr_prudemment_adv.hook: Like English 'prudently', said prew-dah-MAHN: an acrobat PRUDENTLY tests the trapeze with one toe before swinging.

fr_peniblement_adv.hook: A man pushes a huge boulder uphill WITH GREAT DIFFICULTY, groaning with pain ("pay-NEE-bluh").

fr_rudement_adv.hook: A rude man ("rew-duh-MAHN") shoves another ROUGHLY, who stumbles.

fr_solennellement_adv.hook: Like English 'solemnly', said soh-lah-neh-luh-MAHN: a penguin sits SOLEMNLY on a red velvet cushion beside a golden trophy.
fr_solennellement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the penguin sits beside the trophy on its cushion.

fr_severement_adv.hook: Like English 'severely', said say-veh-ruh-MAHN: the ringmaster frowns SEVERELY at a monkey wearing his top hat.

fr_gracieusement_adv.hook: Like English 'gracefully', said grah-syeuh-zuh-MAHN: a hippo in a pink tutu tiptoes GRACEFULLY along a low tightrope.

fr_radicalement_adv.hook: Like English 'radically', said rah-dee-kah-luh-MAHN: a clown has shaved off half his orange wig: a RADICALLY new look in the mirror.

fr_rigoureusement_adv.hook: Like English 'rigorously', said ree-goo-reuh-zuh-MAHN: the ringmaster measures a seal RIGOROUSLY with a long ruler.
fr_rigoureusement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows the seal itself being measured. Example sentence replaced: the source example was about smoking.
ex: Il est rigoureusement interdit de nourrir les animaux.
Feeding the animals is strictly forbidden.

fr_aisement_adv.hook: An easy-going man ("ay-zay-MAHN") holds a grand piano up EASILY on one finger, whistling.

fr_gratuitement_adv.hook: Like English 'gratuitously', said grah-twee-tuh-MAHN: a clown hands out balloons FOR FREE, and a giraffe helps itself to some.

fr_ouvertement_adv.hook: Like English 'overtly', said oo-vehr-tuh-MAHN: a cat yawns OPENLY, mouth wide open for all to see.
fr_ouvertement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted cat yawns with its mouth wide open.

fr_pele_mele_adv.hook: Like English 'pell-mell', said pehl-MEHL: clowns tumble out of a tiny car PELL-MELL, any old how.

fr_systematiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'systematically', said sees-tay-mah-tee-kuh-MAHN: a seal works SYSTEMATICALLY through a box of balls, one after another.

fr_typiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'typically', said teep-kuh-MAHN: TYPICALLY, the clown slips on the banana peel, again tonight.

fr_volontairement_adv.hook: Like English 'voluntarily', said voh-lohn-teh-ruh-MAHN: a brave rabbit hops VOLUNTARILY into the magician's top hat.

fr_artificiellement_adv.hook: Like English 'artificially', said ahr-tee-fee-syeh-luh-MAHN: a lion's ARTIFICIAL mane slips off its strap, revealing a sheepish tabby cat.
fr_artificiellement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows the tabby in the slipping fake mane.

fr_consciemment_adv.hook: Like English 'consciously', said kohn-syah-MAHN: a trapeze cat chooses each grip CONSCIOUSLY, eyes wide open, fully awake.

fr_consciencieusement_adv.hook: Like English 'conscientiously', said kohn-syahn-syeuh-zuh-MAHN: an ant sweeps every grain of sawdust CONSCIENTIOUSLY.

fr_financierement_adv.hook: Like English 'financially', said fee-nahn-syeh-ruh-MAHN: a pig counts coins into a piggy bank: FINANCIALLY, the circus is saved.

fr_indirectement_adv.hook: Like English 'indirectly', said an-dee-rehk-tuh-MAHN: a ball bounces round INDIRECTLY before bopping the clown on the nose.

fr_individuellement_adv.hook: Like English 'individually', said an-dee-vee-dweh-luh-MAHN: three poodles bow INDIVIDUALLY, each in its own spotlight.

fr_intentionnellement_adv.hook: Like English 'intentionally', said an-tahn-syoh-neh-luh-MAHN: a clown trips over his own big shoe ON PURPOSE, grinning and waving at the crowd.

fr_scientifiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'scientifically', said syahn-tee-fee-kuh-MAHN: a monkey in a lab coat SCIENTIFICALLY measures the trampoline with a measuring stick.

fr_distraitement_adv.hook: Like English 'distractedly', said dees-treh-tuh-MAHN: a bear in a striped shirt juggles DISTRACTEDLY, and his lunch sandwich has ended up in the air with the clubs.
fr_distraitement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted juggler is a bear.

fr_fraichement_adv.hook: A fresh-faced baker ("freh-shuh-MAHN") carries a loaf FRESHLY baked, still steaming.

fr_instantanement_adv.hook: Like English 'instantaneously', said ans-tahn-tah-nay-MAHN: the magician snaps his fingers and the dove vanishes INSTANTLY, leaving only a curl of white magic mist in the air.
fr_instantanement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: Reworded to match the painting: the painted dove is gone and only a curl of white mist is left.

fr_momentanement_adv.hook: Like English 'momentarily', said moh-mahn-tah-nay-MAHN: the lamp went out MOMENTARILY, and when it flicked back on the elephant was wearing a pink tutu.
fr_momentanement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the lamp beside the elephant shows the lights going off and on.

fr_parallelement_adv.hook: Like English 'parallel', said pah-rah-lehl-MAHN: a boy drives his toy train along two PARALLEL rails that never meet.
fr_parallelement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows one train on its parallel rails (no dog).

fr_simultanement_adv.hook: Like English 'simultaneously', said see-mewl-tah-nay-MAHN: three acrobats leap SIMULTANEOUSLY, all in mid-air at the same moment.
fr_simultanement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no pyramid is painted, just the joint leap.

fr_soudainement_adv.hook: Like English 'suddenly', said soo-deh-nuh-MAHN: SUDDENLY the cannon fires with a puff, and a clown pops out, still clutching his popcorn.

fr_spontanement_adv.hook: Like English 'spontaneously', said spohn-tah-nay-MAHN: the audience SPONTANEOUSLY breaks into a conga, dancing round the conga drums.
fr_spontanement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted dancers are next to conga drums.

fr_subitement_adv.hook: SUDDENLY a beetroot pops up out of the soup in front of Sue ("sew-beet-MAHN"), and she jumps a mile.
fr_subitement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the beetroot has no face in the painting.

fr_eperdument_adv.hook: A snowman ("MAHN") is DESPERATELY, PASSIONATELY in love with a pear ("ay-PEHR") glistening with dew ("DEW"), and serenades it on his guitar.

fr_etroitement_adv.hook: A pony at a trot ("ay-TRWAHT-mahn") squeezes NARROWLY between two hay bales, its sides just brushing them.

fr_imperativement_adv.hook: Like English 'imperatively', said an-pay-rah-tee-vuh-MAHN: the tiger must be fed IMPERATIVELY now, so the keeper rushes over with a bucket of fish.

fr_intensement_adv.hook: Like English 'intensely', said an-tahn-say-MAHN: a tightrope walker on a low rope stares INTENSELY ahead.

fr_prematurement_adv.hook: Like English 'prematurely', said pray-mah-tew-ray-MAHN: the confetti cannon fires PREMATURELY, covering a startled clown before the act.

fr_temporairement_adv.hook: Like English 'temporarily', said tahn-poh-reh-ruh-MAHN: a cracked, taped-up tent pole is held up TEMPORARILY by an open umbrella until the new one arrives.

fr_stratageme_noun.hook: Like English 'stratagem', said strah-tah-ZHEHM: the magician shows off his 'empty' birdcage while secretly lifting the blue tablecloth, where the white dove hides in a hidden drawer: a sly STRATAGEM.
fr_stratageme_noun.why: RECS p11 plan-move to R_adv_manner_06 (cirque/magie); painted by MKT-B on the empty magician's table.
